Commentary.Commentary: Pakistan's bowlers were once again off the boil! They did not begin that well when the conditions favored them and later on they could not stop the run flow. Imad and Abbas Afridi were good but the rest were taken for plenty. Now they face a big task ahead. Can they gun it down? They do have the batters but Ireland, will back themselves to defend this. Join us for the chase once the rain stops.

The players now run off as the rain keeps coming down! Ireland have a massive score on hand. They lost their openers early but Lorcan Tucker and Harry Tector steadied the ship with a fine stand. Tector fell but Tucker continued. He scored a fine half ton and the rest played around him. George Dockrell and Gareth Delany played excellent cameos to take them to over 190!

... MATCH DAY ....

It is time for the second match of the three-game T20I series between Ireland and Pakistan at Castle Avenue in Dublin. Pakistan face a quick turnaround after suffering a surprising defeat in the series opener, while Ireland are riding high on confidence and aiming to clinch the series with another victory in the second game. In the first T20I, Pakistan had a slow start in the Powerplay but managed to finish strongly, posting a total of 182. However, Andrew Balbirnie spearheaded Ireland's chase, and with contributions from other batters, they managed to clinch a historic victory with a ball to spare, marking their first T20I win against Pakistan. Despite Paul Stirling and Lorcan Tucker failing to make an impact with the bat for Ireland, Andy Balbirnie, Harry Tector, and George Dockrell stepped up, providing them with a significant confidence boost heading into the second match. With the ball, Craig Young was the standout performer, but the other pacers, like Mark Adair, Barry McCarthy, Curtis Campher, and leggie Ben White, struggled and will be looking to improve their performance. As for Pakistan, Babar Azam and Saim Ayub were among the runs in the first match, but it will require a collective effort from the likes of Mohammad Rizwan, Fakhar Zaman, and Azam Khan if Pakistan are to level the series. Additionally, the setback suffered in the first match was compounded by Naseem Shah's injury, who walked off the field in the final over while trying to save a boundary. Pakistan fans will be hoping for his fitness ahead of this crucial game, especially with the T20 World Cup on the horizon. Imad Wasim and Shaheen Afridi were economical with the ball, but the likes of Abbas Afridi and Shadab Khan will need to step up to support them effectively. Will Pakistan put on a spirited performance and force a series decider? We shall find out.
